utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are no preliminaries, therefore could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, Mr. Lukic, in view of the fact that the next witness may be waiting, could you tell us, would you need the whole of the day or would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I need the whole day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You need the whole of the day which means that the next witness doesn't have to remain standby here. That may be of interest for you to know, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Your Honour. We have asked the witness to be on standby at the hotel this afternoon should things change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Even that seems to not be necessary at this moment if Mr. Lukic needs -- even if he would not need the whole of the day, but the greatest part of it, and with re-examination and there's hardly any chance that the next witness would start his testimony today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We'll take appropriate measures now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Meanwhile there is a Defence request for extended response time on the Prosecution's 12th Rule 92 bis motion. That motion was filed on the 28th of January. On the 8th of February, the Defence requested an additional 30 days to respond, and the Chamber grants this request for an extension of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning -- good morning, Mr. Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Suljevic, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will continue where we left off yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 65 ter 10166 to start with.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You know what the document is about, because we discussed it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go to page 3 to remind ourselves of the schematic. We discussed that yesterday, but now I would like to go to page 2 in B/C/S and in English. We're on page 3 now, but I would kindly ask for page 2 to be displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document describes the trajectory of the said projectile, and in the third line from the top it says the missile ricochetted off the gravel surface of the roof, flew over the corner above Studio C, struck and ricochetted off the wall between the first and the second floor of the building where foreign reporters' offices are located, and fell next to a wall of Studio C. The missile exploded on the floor of the passage. This corresponds to what we saw in the schematic, the description, that is; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to call up 65 ter number 14206. I'm interested in page 3 in both -- both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this is the place where the projectile struck Studio C, the place of impact; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now we need page 6. It seems that in e-court there's a mismatch in the page number. Can I go back one page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is an arrow which marks the place where the projectile struck before it ricochetted toward Studio C; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to call up 1D768. It is another photo. I need page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now I will kindly ask you to look at the photo, and can you see where the ricochet place is behind the man in front of the photo?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that. Also -- also I do suppose that it would be somewhere over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in, please. In the place behind the men closest to the camera. The place between the men's legs, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There behind him, exactly behind him, do you see the place marked as the place from which the shell ricochetted? Do you remember that place?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the place, but I'm afraid I can't see the exact spot. It is covered by that individual. Perhaps my sight is not that good.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, then, let's go back to the original the way we saw the first time it was displayed on the screen. Please mark the Energoinvest Dalekovod factory in this photo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, for the Chamber to be able to follow at all, in which direction is the photograph taken, and are we facing north, south, east, west? Or you can also ask the witness about the sketch and see how this relates to the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Usually I know exactly in which direction, but for this photo I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if you could relate it to the sketch we've seen earlier about the drawing. Then to know which roof we are looking at in which direction and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I will clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Suljevic, the roof, the passage, what does that belong to?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm still receiving interpretation. Could you please hold on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you still not receive interpretation in your own language, Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am receiving interpretation, but the only thing I heard was what it belongs to, but I don't know what "it" is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think the witness is now receiving interpretation again. Yes. He is nodding yes, so it seems okay. Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you kindly tell us about this roof, the place where all these individuals are? What does that belong to?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's part of the Radio Television building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the Energoinvest Dalekovod factory in this photo and can you also mark the direction north for us if you can.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to say the schematic that we saw a while ago was drafted by the CSB, not me. Just for the sake of clarity. Here you can see the power transmission lines, Energoinvest tested them. The factory itself is a bit to the right as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark the Energoinvest building with a letter E, and can you please try and tell us where the direction north is in this photo?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is north, because the building faces east-west.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To avoid any confusion because E is Energoinvest and also the notation for east, could you please put the letters ENE.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's assume that the explosion happened or, rather, that the ricochet happened exactly behind the person who is closest to the camera. Can you please draw the descent line of the projectile in the direction of Studio C.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can do it only approximately. [Marks]. I believe that this would be the trajectory of that projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How are we going to mark that? Let's mark it with a letter C, showing that its trajectory is towards Studio C. And also can you draw a line towards Safeta Hadzica 52. Can you get your bearings in the photo and try to do that for us. Can you draw a line towards the Svrakino settlement?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would go from the left across this part of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please put letters SH next to that line standing for Safeta Hadzica.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be preserved? If you have questions, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we wait for a second first. First of all, I lost half of my microphone. But apart from that -- could we first look at the map and see where exactly we are. Could you use some of the -- yes, we can save this first, perhaps. Madam Registrar. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. The Prosecution would just inquire when this photo was taken. The probative value of it may be impacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first -- before we change anything, let's first save this picture. Madam Registrar, the photograph marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D203, Your Honours. Apologies, D204, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D204. Any objection against it being admitted, Mr. Weber, although you would like to know when it was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. D204 is admitted. Now, the question was when the photograph was taken. Do you know, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, does the witness know? If not, of course you can't give evidence, but you can say something about the source of your material you're using.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This photo was taken during the official tour by the Trial Chamber in a case of General Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, I had a look at the date of that. I was just hoping to put the date of it on the record if Mr. Lukic knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I have the number. It's pretty long number, taken by -- from the site of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. Give -- if the number is long, write it down on a piece of paper and give it to Mr. Weber so that he can check it on the -- Second, where are we on the Sarajevo map so that we have a better impression? You can use Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have one photo. If maybe we can use it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was talking about a map first because maps have the advantage that you know where you are. We have an mp3. We have a detailed map of Sarajevo divided into 16. It's hard copy page 58. Could you tell us where we should go in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have that map with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please briefly explain and then we get the right one. Where are we? Are we in Dobrinja? Are we anywhere between the town and Dobrinja? Are we near Alipasino Polje? Where approximately are we? Where's the Energo --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the building of Television Sarajevo on the main street leading from SUP to Bascarsija. It is in Novo Sarajevo part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. Is it closer to town than Alipasino Polje or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably witness can guide us more precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us the building we're looking at at this moment, that is the television building, Television Sarajevo, where do we find it approximately on the map? Could you guide us? Is it west of the city centre, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is closest to Alipasino Polje. This is the beginning of Alipasino Polje or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have -- sheet 10 is hard copy page 68 of P3, but it's a different page in e-court. I'm aware of that. Let's see. Mr. Weber, could you tell us where sheet 10 is in the e-court pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: E-court page 75.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have P3, page 75. Perhaps we use the whole of the screen for the map. Witness, do we find the television building on this part of the map? If not, please tell us whether we have to go east, west, north, or south. If you'd like to have it enlarged, we'll enlarge it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It does not have to be enlarged, but just bear with me for a moment. Yes. This is the part of the map depicting the Radio Television building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I saw that you had -- you started marking already. We see that the river Miljacka is crossing the street. That's where you made a marking. Now, is the television building, is that on the southern part? Is that south of the road or is it north of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will mark the Radio Television building now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would not mind, then I notice that's the Radio Television building. That is a -- you've marked that now. That is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both in the north and in the east, the river Miljacka flows along at that building. Now we know where we are. The photograph with the Energoinvest building is taken in which building? Is that taken east or is that taken in a westerly direction? Towards the east or towards the west?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can draw an arrow to show you what I think about the direction from which the photo was taken. I believe that this is the direction from which the photo was taken, but I suppose it was taken from the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I invite you to erase again the arrow you've made at this moment. I noticed yesterday that you know how to do it. Yes. Thank you. And could you please mark from that building with an arrow in which direction the photographer was taking its picture, or another way is to tell us where the Energo building is, if it is on this part of the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I wasn't there when the photo was taken. However, from memory about the position of the building and the adjacent building, I believe that I can give you some sort of an idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you go -- if you go from this television building to the Energoinvest building, you are travelling away from the city. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. Now I marked the place where the power transmission lines are, the ones that can be seen in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That may be very helpful, because we have -- on our map we have indicated towers and that may be electricity towers. Now we know approximately where we are, Mr. Lukic, we can perhaps go back to the photograph after we have stored this marked map. Shall we make a D exhibit? That's the easiest. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Page 75 of the Exhibit P3 as marked by the witness receives number D205, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now misuse the Presiding Judge's efforts, so I will ask you to use this same map of the city which is properly shown with the north, south, east, and west, and I will ask you to draw on it the building of the Radio Television, if you can, and also the address Safeta Hadzica 52, if you can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness has marked the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the building of the radio and television.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark Svrakino Selo as well?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Svrakino Selo, yes, but not the street and the house number. [Marks]. It's thereabouts in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So that's to the south from the television building; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The advantage of this map, Mr. Lukic, is that, for example, Safeta Hadzica is just written down nicely on the map, and the witness has marked it approximately at that street. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would propose this marked sketch with markings made by Mr. Suljevic to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D206, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please show another sketch, 1D745.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, would this sketch actually correspond to what we saw, how there was this ricocheting from the roof. This place is marked with R2. Then impact in the building and the explosion against the wall of Studio C?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the trajectory more or less corresponds -- or, rather, the direction, but as for the trajectory itself, I'm not sure how the projectile was flying, so I cannot confirm whether this was the precise trajectory that it flew along. We can only speculate about that, about the trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we are looking at this, I will just read once again what 10166 says. That's a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, let's try to be very precise. You say the ricochet -- the first one was on the roof. Is that R1?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: R1 is the ricochet on the roof. R2 apparently is where --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is another ricochet from the building --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at least where the projectile --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the wall, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- was stopped by a wall and went in the other direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, we do not know at this moment how the cut is taken as far as the buildings is concerned, neither do we know what the dotted line means, and we have no measurements, that is, whether the altitude of the -- the size of the building, length, or the -- how high the building was, it's not anywhere presented. I don't know who made this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll have Mr. Berko Zecevic testify here, and he testified before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He measured the distance, and I will give it to the witness and read one portion from the document we have already read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's all fine, because we do not see any of it on this picture, but please then proceed and keep in the back of your mind what I'd like to know looking at this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like also to ask a question. When this projectile ricochetted on R1, where did it come from? Are we able to know the direction from where it came? Further to the right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can ask the witness if he knows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has explained, I think that only with a very acute angle of descent you can have a ricochet, so I even whether -- wonder how it ricochetted would fit into that, but it must therefore logically come from the right although it's not indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can read what we have in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In what document, this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- let's proceed, but logically - and, Witness, if you would disagree, please tell me - but logically in view of the arrows, it could only have come from the right, and what direction that is, we do not know because we do not know how the cut through the building was made. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we already read this a little while ago. On page 2 of 10166 reads as follows: The projectile bounced off or ricochetted against the gravel surface of the roof, flew above the corner of Studio C, hit and bounced off from the wall between the first and the second floors of the building where offices of foreign reporters were located, and fell directly by the wall of Studio C. The projectile was activated on the floor of the passage. Would you agree with me that the sketch represents exactly what the document says, what I have just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only I said that the red line is probably approximate and we can accept it as such, because 1 would be the place where the projectile hit the gravel roof, and what is missing is the part of the red line showing where the projectile came from. It probably or, rather, must have come from the right side. It hit at R1, then hit and bounced off the wall from R2 and hit next to the fence. Now, whether it rolled on the ground or hit the wall of Studio C, these are the details that we can only guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you would also agree with me, and the witness would also, that, for example, indications as it hit between this and that floor without any floors on the sketch, we do not know whether it was at the fifth floor or at the tenth or depending on how many floors there were in these buildings, but the sketch does not represent all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't, Your Honour, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But let's proceed meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Let us now return then briefly to 14206 [Realtime transcript read in error "12406"]. I think that we were looking at page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many floors the TV building has? We see once again the place marked with an arrow which is represented as the location of the second ricochet, represented by R2 in the other sketch.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building of the RTV has a number of levels, so this part of the roof with gravel, I'm not sure whether it's the third or the fourth floor, and the place where the projectile hit is the second higher part of the building which has perhaps eight or nine floors. I don't know exactly, but it's much taller. So the building is constructed in such a way that it has varying levels, but how many floors exactly it has I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It reads here that it hit between the first and the second floors of the building.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then it's possible that the flat part which is lower -- the place of the first ricochet was three or four floors. I don't know exactly, but it's much lower than the central part of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all not reflected on the sketch difference of sizes of the building, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it would be possible if the trajectory, that this line of that shows that the projectile is 15 metres. It was said that it should be 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What should be 15 metres exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From R1 to R2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, whether it should be or not, of course, the Chamber is primarily interested in what it was, but we have at this moment not seen on the photograph yet the exact place where the projectile ricochetted, and all the measurements are not on the sketch you've given us. Perhaps on the first sketch I do remember that there are far more details as far as measurements are concerned, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you want, we can go back to that 10166, page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we could look at it very briefly, and then I'll let you further go, but please keep in mind that in order to get a proper understanding of the situation, that -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Lukic, if I may interrupt. When you asked for us to look at this sketch which is 14206, you asked for 14206, and the transcript at page 15, line 1, has it as 12406. I just wanted to make sure that we've got the right number before it disappears.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, right, Your Honour. It's 14206.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may tell you how I see it. You can see the roof in one part and it says P2, so I suppose it's the ground floor plus two floors of the flat section of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is how it is usually marked in our parts at least. Do you also see in this sketch what is the distance between the place of the first ricochet to the place of the second ricochet? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, never mind, then. We'll have to wait for Mr. Zecevic to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Can we now please see 1D743.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just say that this is a document that you signed together with Mr. Jamakovic, dated the 17th of July, 1995, and the document discusses this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document has not been translated, or at least we haven't found a translation. We have sent it for translation, though, and I will just show by way of this document that Mr. Suljevic dealt with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, yesterday the Prosecution continued to look for any available translations of a copy of this document and we were able to locate almost complete translation except for the last page of the report and we did send that to Mr. Lukic yesterday. It's not a -- the currently uploaded version of the last page is fully legible. The version that we had the translation for the last page was not fully legible so that was what was incomplete.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have that on the e-court, then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it uploaded in e-court by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We did not. We provided it for Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. That's the answer. Mr. Lukic, you have not uploaded it into e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't know that there was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that you either upload it in e-court during the next break and that we then further look at it, or that's an alternative possibility that you print out the pages you want to use in the English translation so that we can follow it. Either of the two would do, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We'll try to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then perhaps if you then put questions to the witness so that we are --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can see this document and do you remember that you were doing this on the 28th of June? The first paragraph reads the request says that on the 28th of June, 1995, around 0922 hours in the 6th Proleterske Brigade Street number 4, on the RTV building in Novi Grad municipality, a projectile fell and exploded, killing one person and injuring 30 and causing considerable material damage. So you did work on this incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have a courtesy copy of the English translation if you'd like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I think Mr. Lukic read almost literally from this third paragraph in the -- which describes the date and the explosion. Thank you very much, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's just one copy that we were able to print out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have one document, and -- yes, please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we just need the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up in the top of the page, three paragraphs from the end, I'm not sure what it looks like in the English because I haven't seen the English version, it says "Enclosure" and then two paragraphs above that it reads: On the basis of the materials submitted for the expert analysis and examination, it has been established that this is a destructive air bomb probably weighing 250 kilogrammes. The mass of the explosive charge in the bombs of this type is 96 kilogrammes. It also says that the bomb was most probably attached to rocket engines, and it says that the fragments of those rocket engines have not been found, which you already told us. So an air bomb of 250 kilogrammes, together with the engines, probably weighs around 300 kilogrammes, and with the parts that attach the engines to the body of the bomb; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably even more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the velocity of these bombs is around 150 metres in second or -- per second or 540 kilometres per hour; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not engage in those analyses, so I can neither confirm nor deny that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Would you agree with me that this report is actually a report about an impossible trajectory, that the bomb having such mass with such velocity after ricocheting against the wall would not explode there but would change the trajectory once again and all of that at a distance of 15 metres. Having the knowledge of mechanics as you do, would you be able to confirm this report or would you say that it's rather impossible?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the report that I made? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I read to you just a while ago, that this was actually the trajectory of the bomb.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't want to speculate, but I suppose that approximately that was most probably the trajectory of the bomb. What we don't know is whether the bomb was set to explode immediately or was there supposed to be a later explosion, whether it was a timed bomb. So this is something that we don't know and that we cannot determine in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you determine what the fuse was like on this bomb? Did you look into that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not find any traces of the fuse, at least not any traces that would indicate to us what was the fuse that made this air bomb complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, while this was within 30 seconds and the break is soon so that you have a further opportunity to consult.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, on the bombs which you showed to us in images which we looked at yesterday, the Prosecution presented you that, I mean those that were found in Lukavica, did you determine what types of fuses were used in those bombs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the bombs that were found in Ilijas --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then it was my mistake. I suppose in Ilijas.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You said Lukavica, but it was in Ilijas. I did not analyse those bombs, but one electronic scheme was brought to the department, the team which was in charge of that brought the mechanical and electronic wiring that was part of this bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what the fuse was? What was brought?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you that this was the mechanic and electronic wiring which included the clock mechanism and there were other elements, too, but I did not really analyse it in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you wouldn't agree with me that this explosion was actually set there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would move to Safeta Hadzica, and we will need in e-court P495.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we get too afield on a different incident, I was just wondering if counsel plans on tendering 65 ter 10166 and 1D743, which we've now had multiple reference from the witness with during the course of his testimony. I appreciate that with respect to 1D743 that we need a completed translation. Maybe if that could be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whatever we've used we plan to tender, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Shall we do it right away and then move after the break to the next subject. If you give the 65 -- if you give the numbers, Mr. Lukic, then I'll invite Madam Registrar to assign numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10166 receives number D207, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and just for my information, that was, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That was the sketch of the RTV building. That was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The sketch of the RTV building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And it has an attached legend that Mr. Lukic also showed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. No objections. I take it D207 is admitted. Next one, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Next one was 1D743, Your Honours, and this receives number D208, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for my information, that was --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was the report authored by the witness in relation to the shelling of the RTV building on the 28th of June. If we could have that marked for identification pending the completion of the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the report. Could I draw your attention to the following. I think as it is uploaded now in the original, first of all, the last page is quite well legible, so therefore from that version also the last page could be translated. But there are other matters attached which do not appear in the one you have uploaded in the original. I see in the translation at least one additional page photocopy of topographic map, et cetera, et cetera, and then it looks as if reference is made to all kind of photographs or the object marked number 2, for example, is described, the object marked number 3, so apparently there must be more in that document. Could the parties either agree that we don't need it, but for us to read it, we'd like to know what it refers to. So completing and the document and the translation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. And the Prosecution also forgot that the Defence did use --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first for this moment, Madam Registrar, the document which is -- no, there's nothing on the screen anymore. The document which is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 1D00743 would reserve -- would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D208, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D208 and is marked for identification. And then the next one, Mr. -- and to be completed and to be fully translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, the Defence also used the photo file related to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 14206. Judge Moloto warned us about the wrong number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, and that would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 14206 receives number D209, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D209 is admitted into evidence. I still have 1D745 on my list which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the that sketch we created but -- R1 and R2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, with the red suggested trajectory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- we would have an objection to this being admitted for its substantive value. Much like last week, I believe a similar sketch was shown for demonstrative purposes, pending any foundation as to the accuracy of it and addressing the concerns raised by the Chamber, we'd have no objection to it being marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did I understand you well that it will be further discussed with a witness Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that one will be marked for identification under what number, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D745 will be MFI'd as number D210, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D210 is marked for identification. We take a break. Could the witness fault usher. Apologies, Mr. Suljevic, for bothering you with all this administrative matters, but unfortunately, it is necessary. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While the witness is being brought in, can I bring something to the Chamber's attention. Last week the Prosecution filed a draft notice of the remaining witnesses in its case. The Prosecution has not included in that list witnesses that the Prosecution no longer believes it's necessary to adduce their evidence in reliance on the Chamber's adjudicated facts decisions. Over the course of the March adjournment, the Prosecution will be formally filing a list of those witnesses and the adjudicated facts upon which we rely. The reason I raise it now is that Mr. Lukic and the Chamber have made reference to Mr. Berko Zecevic and that questions may be put to him. At present it is not our intention to call him, but to rely on adjudicated facts. That could change over the course of the spring, but at present that's our intention. So I wouldn't want Mr. Lukic to falsely rely on a witness that may not be called and, you know, not put questions to this witness that -- with that intention. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If it is the intention of the Defence through Mr. Berko Zecevic to challenge those adjudicated facts covered by his statement, then of course it would be good to know that as early as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you to my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then meanwhile, I also use the time for a decision on Defence request for an extended respond time in relation to Rule 92 ter motion for Witness RM174. That motion was filed on the 25th of January, and on the 30th of January, the Prosecution was requested to refile it. The Defence filed a motion on the 8th of February requesting an extension of 14 days to respond starting from the date of the Prosecution's refiling of the motion. Mr. Groome, do we know already when you expect to refile the motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can inform the Chamber at the end of this session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll wait with that until the end of this session. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Suljevic, I would like us to focus on the developments at Safeta Hadzica 52 and some adjacent numbers, 102, 105, 110. We find this in your statement on page 9, paragraph 53, where that's in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now we will need P495. The document has been removed from the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Again just for the record, document is under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the case in question. Reports were drafted by the Sarajevo CSB, as well as the KDZ department, i.e., your department. We have a document that you drafted on the same case. Do you remember that particular incident?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were the expert who analysed the traces after the explosion?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us try and get our bearings first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In e-court we need 18833, which is a Prosecutor's exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this photo please try and get your bearings. Somewhere in the middle is the Bosnian and Herzegovinian Radio and Television building. Could you please mark it. Do you recognise that building, first of all?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the place where the projectile ricochetted? Can you recognise the place on the roof?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can do it more or less accurately. It would be somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. We agree on that. And can you now mark the building at Safeta Hadzica Street 52. Can you locate that building in this photo.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. I believe that it is one of these buildings. I don't know exactly which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on the right-hand side. That's number 52. And do you know where number 102 is?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could we invite the witness to write TV next to the small marking and 52 next to the big circular marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you kindly put letters TV next to the circle indicating the television building.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can you put numbers 52 next to the other circle. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted as the next Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 18833 receives number D211, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now we need P495, under seal, once again. We're interested in page 10 in this document in B/C/S. And we need page 11 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature in the B/C/S version, sir?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your report, which is now in front of us, you did not mention the type of bomb; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. There is no reference to the type of bomb because it was not established. There were no traces which would identify the type of bomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Thank you. Likewise, you did not know how many engines it may have had, the GRAD-type engines; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could only assume based on the traces which were supplied to us, and we could not be precise in respect of the number of engines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many chambers does one engine have? How many traces -- how many chambers would you have been able to find if there was just one engine?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A rocket engine equals one chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In other words, this was your calculation: If you find one chamber, there's one engine.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you find a rocket engine body, that equals one rocket --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about chambers. How many chambers does one engine have?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I believe it was one chamber only, because it is all encompassed within one rocket engine body with jets, and we established the number of rockets based on the bodies of rocket engines that were delivered for the expert analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now we're still talking about the same incident and the same day according to this report issued by the Sarajevo centre CSB. Several dozens of artillery projectiles fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D697. I believe that it already has a number, but if not, it is 1D697. The same photo may be found on page 5 of P497. It is photo 5 on page 5, but our photo here is of better quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, this is Safeta Hadzica 102, the place of impact. Could you please mark the place where the projectile struck the building.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you also draw the paw, the remains of shrapnel in the wall, in other words.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the density of the shrapnel is the highest. This is what remains after the projectile exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you explained to us that the shrapnel disperses in the direction from which the shell came.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we conclude based on the photo that the mortar shell, therefore, came from the bottom of the building?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that this was a mortar shell. However, the projectile which struck the wall most probably fell under an angle which was below the horizontal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us that in layman terms. Did the projectile come from above or from below?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The projectile -- I don't know what its trajectory was. We cannot say that it came from above or from below. When it hit the surface, the projectile was below the horizontal level, i.e., the position of the projectile was below the horizontal level. We cannot say where it was fired from, whether it was from above the place of impact or below it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "below the horizontal level," are you saying that the tail of that projectile was lower than its front part?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the moment of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see 1D750 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should we have this one marked first --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- admit it having -- Madam Registrar, the photograph marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Photograph 1D697 as marked by the witness receives number D212, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D212 is admitted into evidence, and this is the same photograph which was marked by the witness earlier and was admitted as D172.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Different witness, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Different witness, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Now we need 1D750. While we are waiting for this photograph to show up on the screen, we can also find the same one in P497, the first photograph on the first page, but this one is of a better quality, and it's easier to discern what we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the place marked as the place where the projectile fell into the yard of Safeta Hadzica 102. To get our bearings, the red roof is the roof of the police station in Prvomajska Street number 20. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't remember the roof the police station, but I do not deny it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just saying if you know, fine. If you don't, we'll establish that in some other way. Do you know whether there is a police station today in Prvomajska number 20?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's the police station in Prvomajska, probably number 20, but I do not know the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So to this day; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now it's the police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Police administration. All right. Could you please mark the place of the impact of the projectile on this photograph. Can one see it at all?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with certainty. You can see how the ground is not flat, but whether someone was digging there or if it was caused by the projectile, but probably if it was there and if it exploded, it could have been there, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that, but I'm asking you whether you can mark the place of the projectile's impact on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not on the site, but let me try and suppose where it could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Please do suppose.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it has been marked, but the witness said he couldn't know for certain, but if it was anywhere, most likely it would be there. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Would you agree with me that in this photograph one cannot see that either the onions which have been planted here were destroyed nor the sticks which are dug into the ground or the wire fence which is visible in the lower part of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I've been letting this go, but I object to relevance at this time. And we have no idea even if this photo is at or near the time that the incident occurred and now we're going into sticks in the ground and whether or not they were destroyed or not, things of that nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the basis for your question is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have this photograph offered by the Prosecution in their admitted Exhibit P497 at page 1, photo 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are just offering better photo because that one was murky and nothing could be seen. On this photo we want to test with this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber -- but I don't think the problem is the photo. The problem is that the witness says he has difficulties in establishing whether or not this is an impact of a shell, and you say the onions are not damaged. I do not know whether there are any onions also on the place where the witness marked, because you could say that there's no onion left, but we do not know whether there were ever any onions there, but the onions at a distance of 2 to 3 metres seem not to have undergone major -- it's all rather speculative. But come to your point as quickly as possible but with such a level of certainty that it assists the Chamber. Yes. And if it is the same photograph of better quality, could the parties - I'm looking both left and right - tell us when it was taken? Was it immediately after the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the same photograph, Your Honours, only brought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- brought to the Tribunal but by one of the Prosecutor's witnesses later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I just ask you to help us to -- we have no clear recollection at this moment when the photograph was taken, but I think it was a photograph attached to an incident report upon investigation almost immediately after the event. That is what my recollection tells me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, your recollection is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And you said it was part of P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P497. Please proceed. Come to your point as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you examine the photo file while you were drawing up your own report and opinion?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. While drawing up our report, we had no occasion to see this photograph. I did see this photograph on the last occasion when I testified before this Tribunal, and as for the explosion, one can see the traces of shrapnel on the wall. I mean, these concrete blocks. You can also see that the roof is damaged because the shadows of the rafters can be seen on the wall, and there is a lack of the corrugated surface which covered the roof. So these are the elements that indicate that there was an explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Quite the opposite. We'll try to prove that by the following photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we please see 1D751 in e-court now. [In English} Please, yes. Can we -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Photograph marked by the witness, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D750 as marked by the witness receives number D213, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you for the warning, and thank you to Madam Registrar. Now we need photograph 1D751. It is a photograph included in P497 on page 3, photograph number 3. Once again, this one is of a better quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see here a car. Would you agree with me that the car is parked next to the same building and the same garden we saw on the previous photograph, which is 1D750?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's zoom in and look at 1D752. This photograph is once again included in P497, photograph 4 on page 4, but the photograph that we are showing now is of a higher quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see anywhere in this photograph that there was an impact of shrapnel, or would you agree with me that this is rather a bomb that was planted, that the explosive which was under the hood of the car in the engine is the one that actually exploded?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, is it your suggestion that this photograph is the same as we find on page 3 or another page of --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- page --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't speculate, because I was not there, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you worked with explosives. Is this a typical photograph showing that the explosive was planted below the hood? You can see the parts of the gears to the right from the windscreen and also below the windscreen.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's obvious that the explosion did occur in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mean in an enclosed space below the hood?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, thereabouts. I cannot specify without doing a detailed analysis and an on-site investigation. On the basis of a photograph, there are few indications that would tell us all this. It's certain that there was an explosion, but I wouldn't speculate what caused it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that neither in the previous photograph nor on this one can we see any traces of the car's hood?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this one we cannot see it on the car. Whether it's somewhere to the side of the car, I'm not sure. If we could have a look again at the previous photograph so that we can try to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please once again see 1D751, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you notice anywhere on this car -- you can see the front left side of the car, so can you see any traces of shrapnel there or on the roof or anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are some black dots which I notice, but I cannot claim whether it's that or not just on the basis of this photograph. Some black dots both on the roof and on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, of course there was an explosion, but can you see that the column next to the driver is twisted to the right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the entire chassis is obviously deformed because of the explosion. That is obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The licence plate numbers of the car are mentioned here but not photographed. Do you have any information as to why?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the same day, the same incident, but a different shell, so we need 1D754. Once again, we are offering a better photograph, but it can be found within P497, page 7, photograph number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the crater allegedly made by a projectile. It is noted that it fell in the schoolyard of the Dzemaludin Musovic primary school. We even think that the name of the school is not correct. Dzemaludin Musovic was a well-known football player; correct? And the name of the school should have been Dzemaludin Causevic. Are you familiar with the information?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that Dzemaludin Causevic is the name of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have heard of Dzemaludin Musovic, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We all have, all of us who used to live in that area at the time.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only we don't know whether there were others with the name Dzemaludin Musovic even before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. In this photograph can you see, and I will suggest to you -- can you see any characteristic traces of a shell explosion or is this an example of water washing away the ground below asphalt and then the asphalt sinks? Or can you see any traces of an explosion in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once again I wouldn't speculate, because this is a microphotograph, so one cannot see anything that is in the surrounding area around the crater. One can see that a crater was formed, but what caused it, once again I wouldn't speculate about this because I did not visit the site and the photograph doesn't show the general area around the crater which would allow me to see if there any additional traces and the like. Whether the projectile exploded or if it remained unexploded in the ground, we cannot say, and I wouldn't like to express any conjectures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But we may conclude that on this photograph one does not see any traces of an explosion.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We do not see the general area of the crater which would allow us to claim that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness says that he can't make such determinations, and to say you do not see an explosion, of course you never see an explosion itself. You see the traces of an explosion. The witness said that he couldn't -- what we see is apparently what is a hole in what seems to be the ground. The witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] The next document we need to see is 1D753. It's a photograph which can also be found in P497. It's photograph number 9 on page 9 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says that this is a projectile. You will remember that it was mentioned that it had some strange markings, and it says that it fell in Safeta Hadzica Street number 70 and did not explode. Do you remember this projectile?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I said, I did not go to the site, but I remember a similar projectile which -- the traces of which I did analyse and include in a report, but as for this projectile, I did not receive it, nor was I at the site at the moment when this photograph was taken. One can only see on the projectile that it was fired, because on these rings we can see the traces made by the -- made by the firing, and also we can see that the part where the fuse twists it is damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll come back to that. You can also see that the head is damaged; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that the head of the shell is damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now we need P495. The document is under seal. This is an official report which was drafted on the 1st of June by the Sarajevo Security Services Centre. It says here that the projectile -- and it is in both versions. In English it's line 9 on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The projectile which landed in the garden in front of the north-west wall of the apartment building at Safeta Hadzica Street 70 resulted in a 200 by 80 by 35 centimetre crater, and it did not explode. Later on we will also discuss the following sentence, which reads as follows: "The next projectile landed in the middle of Majdanska Street. It ricochetted off the asphalt surface and hit the wall of Dzemaludin Lujinovic's family house." Does this look plausible for you? Is it plausible for this shell to land, not to explode, and to create a crater of this size, 200 by 80 by 35 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again we should start from the assumption as to whether the projectile hit a surface and then went on moving. 200 is possible. When it landed it may have created a crater 200 centimetres wide. The depth that is mentioned here is the deepest, but it is possible that that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When it lands on soft soil, is it normal that the head of the shell breaks?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it didn't break. It was damaged. There was no fuse on the shell. Let me just give you an example. There were cases when we found unexploded shells which were fired without fuses. Either the fuse was not screwed on properly or something else. It did happen. I don't know what happened in this particular case, and the example that I gave you does not apply to this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This specific case - on B/C/S page 2, and in English it is also page 2, paragraph 3 - it says that on the projectile there was some markings with a swastika and also an eagle sign depicting a swastika which was also found on the projectile. Do you remember that? I asked you about that at the beginning, and now I am making a reference to a specific case.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I did not analyse this projectile, but I'm familiar with these details that you've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was also identified as an 88-millimetre projectile. Did you come across shells used by the Army of Republika Srpska of 88-millimetre?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one report everything indicated that the projectile was 88-millimetre, and I found the reference to such shells in professional literature, and based on the traces, I concluded that that was the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're talking about this one in this image?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, an 88-millimetre projectile, German made. We did not have any markings, so I cannot claim for a fact that it was indeed that, but it was an 88-millimetre projectile in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the VRS had barrels through which such projectiles could be fired?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, but this type of shell according to expert statements which we consulted during our analysis can be fired from a 90-millimetre cannon, and the same tables, tables for this type of projectile, can be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 90-millimetre cannons are naval cannons; right? And there were no such cannons around Sarajevo on VRS positions?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I can't testify to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told us that you consulted professional literature relative to ammunition. Do you know that in the JNA there was a regulation on the overhaul of ammunition every 15 to 20 years? So the ammunition that was made before the Second World War or during the war would be overhauled or destroyed. You know that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this photo that we have just seen, did you see traces of a recent overhaul, i.e., that the ammunition was repainted?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't claim that based on any photo. In any case, a projectile which is overhauled has to be marked for that. That has to be specified on a projectile, and based on this photo I can't say anything to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's just go back a little and look at 1D755.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question in relation to the -- what we see on the screen at this moment and tell me immediately if you can't answer the question. This -- the projectiles are described as 90-millimetre armour-piercing explosive artillery projectiles. Could you tell us, armour-piercing explosive artillery projectiles, are they usually provided with a fuse which gives an explosion upon impact or a delayed explosion, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are combined fuses with instant impact and delayed impact. Fuses are adjusted, a certain part is moved so as to make it explode instantly or with a delay. I don't know what the case was with this projectile. In any case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not that on armour-piercing explosive that you usually would use a certain type of fuse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All projectiles had fuses that completed them. One fuse could not be used to complete all projectiles. Some could be used for several different projectiles, and some could be used exclusively for one projectile. In this particular case, I don't know what type of fuse was used. However, if I'm not mistaken, it was a projectile which was intended to pierce armour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I was focusing on specifically, yes. Would that be an indication of what type of fuse to be used with such a projectile?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer this question with any precision. The difference between anti-armour projectiles and other projectiles is that the former hold less explosive and had a higher piercing power. They were used, hence the name, to pierce armour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the Croatian forces had 90-millimetre cannons?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know -- or, rather, I'm not aware of the complete range of armament that the VRS had. I don't even know what the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had. I'm not aware of the full list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us go back to 1D755. This is a photo which can be found on page 10 of P497. It is photo number 10 on page 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see the scratches on this projectile?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does the body of the shell demonstrate that it never went through a barrel?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not put it that way. It would take into account the copper ring on the lower part. You can see that it did go through a barrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At one point. However, if that shell had been fired through a barrel on that occasion, would the traces have been different?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There don't have to be traces at all. Very little is left on the body of the shell. The rotating ring is of a higher diameter than the body of the shell, so that's the place where you would expect more traces to be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How would you account for the vertical lines that we see on the casing of this projectile?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not speculate. It is not my intention to speculate at all. I don't have an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Would you agree with me that a fuse never breaks when an artillery shell lands on the ground.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't have a precise answer to that question. In my opinion, it may break. It depends on the angle of descent, i.e., on the angle of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Even if we're talking about the soil surface?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Unless there is a hard object or a concrete object in the soil. When it comes to that projectile, I could not see a fuse on that projectile, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're putting it to you that that shell was planted. Somebody had kept it in a cellar and then it was planted in order to lay blame on the Serb forces. Could you accept that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would never accept that proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But then how do you account for the shell in this place? Was it ever fired from somewhere?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If -- if it was found in that place, my explanation would be that it was fired like all the other projectiles. As we saw in the previous report, a dozen of projectiles fell in the area over a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
