utterances.text: But there are no traces? There was a building which was targeted from below; is that correct? And then this shell with the German markings made before the Second World War, never overhauled, are all of these shells for which you claim that they were fired?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will move on. We have other examples.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that the shell was never overhauled because I don't know. I didn't say that the projectile was fired from below, because I am not aware of its trajectory from the moment it went through the barrel to the moment it hit the surface, so I don't agree with that. And these are not my conclusions as you're putting it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It's time for our next break. We'll continue after it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break. Could the witness first follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the last session the Chamber asked us some questions with respect to RM174.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I can inform the Chamber that it take some weeks, if not months, to redo the statement as the Chamber has requested us to do. In the schedule, the draft schedule we submitted last week, we have him down for calling him after the summer break. Given -- one of the problems with this particular witness is that given the technical nature of the statement, we're a little bit reluctant to simply have an interpreter translate an English statement. We think it's probably best to have him be working in his own language in the new statement so -- but anyway, that's the schedule the Prosecution imagines. And we, of course, as always, defer to the Chamber on setting the schedule for Defence responses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your position as far as an extension of time is --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As always, Your Honour, we defer to the Chamber and we agree that whatever is necessary to ensure the fair trial rights of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because we recently had -- I think in respect of the refiling of the expert report of Mr. Theunens, you opposed taking the time from the date of refiling, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the difference there is, Your Honour, we believe that all of the information necessary to make an informed decision about their response is before the Defence at this stage. The fact that we may redact a paragraph or several paragraphs in compliance with the Chamber's guidance wouldn't -- I don't believe would affect their ability to make an informed response to that filing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll further consider the matter. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] We would need once again P495 [Realtime transcript read in error "46795"]. Once again it's the official report from the Sarajevo CSB. And this document is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we see at this moment is a P number where luckily we are not yet at. We are not in the 46000 yet. Let's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From this document we need page 2 in English version, paragraph 1, and B/C/S version also page 2, paragraph 1. Somewhere around the middle of this paragraph, in the B/C/S version and in the English version, the last third of this paragraph says: The next projectile ricochetted off the asphalt surface and hit the wall of Dzemaludin Lujinovic's family house in Majdanska Street, exploding on impact and damaging the house. Can we please see 1D759 in e-court. And we can find the same photograph of poorer quality in P497, page 11, photograph 11. [In English] I'm sorry, before I continue, I just want to check whether all our exhibits were on the record. So have we asked for 755 to be admitted, please. No?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we do that now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D755 receives number D214, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D214 is admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then next one we ask to be admitted, 1D752.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have we seen that, Mr. -- we have seen it, and it's not yet tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] You can start at 751.

utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.text: And is admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D217, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You also had 753.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask for that. Yes, 1D753, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D218, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D218 is admitted. Mr. Lukic, 1D759, any --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 759 is on our screen, so I haven't finished that one yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for reminding me anyways. I will forget for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And my colleagues are assisting me as you are aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Suljevic, here in front of us is a photograph relating to Majdanska Street. You can see here next to number 8, on the asphalt, the place which is marked as the one from which the shell ricochetted and then hit the family house up there, also visible on the screen. Could you please mark the location on the asphalt the place where the shell ricochetted and also whether you know what was damaged on the house by the ricochet.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I did not go out on the site, so I'm not familiar with the position or the house or which house was hit or any of that, and on the basis of this photograph, I cannot even guess. It's obvious that there is some sort of damage on the surface next to the number 8, and perhaps we might zoom in so that it would be more easily seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please zoom in. Yes, just like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's visible. The damage on the asphalt is visible. Whether there's anything else in the crater, I don't know that, because I cannot see it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the crater, and mark the material on the right which can also be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the witness said the crater was to the right of number 8, while the Chamber is still able to detect that there is some damage to the surface of the asphalt and that there is some small particles of whatever around. The Chamber is still able to see that even without being guided by the witness, unless you have any specific questions to ask him, but the witness told us --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I -- I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although please keep in mind that the witness said that it's very difficult for him to draw any conclusions or make any observations on the relation of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will ask the witness and if he can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then see, but the marking seems to be unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Suljevic, you can see that all the fragments from the crater are to the right of the supposed location of the ricochet. In your view, is this something normal, that fragments from the surface would all be blown out to the right side?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you be more specific in your question, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first zoom out slightly. Let's first ask whether these are fragments of the crater or not. Let's first ask whether the witness recognises whatever is there on the ground, whether you consider this on the basis of what you see, fragments of the crater. That's the first question. And the second one, whether they're all on the right. Could you answer first that question. What do you see on the surface? Are these fragments of the crater?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the right from number 8 we can see the damage on the asphalt, but I cannot claim what caused it on the basis of this photograph, whether it's the crater made by a projectile that exploded or by a projectile that ricochetted and whether it's just an imprint from the ricocheting of the ordnance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nor could I claim which street this is just on the basis of the photograph, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will have to dwell a bit more on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then please be very concrete, because apparently you see only small fragments of whatever to the right, whereas I see quite a few to the left as well. So therefore, I'm slightly surprised by the question, but if the witness sheds additional light, please put very concrete and precise questions to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your colleagues mention this as the place where the shell ricochetted and that flying from there it damaged the house which we can see on the screen before us. Do you doubt that report, because you say that you can not confirm whether this is that specific street and that specific location?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to speculate. I don't know where the projectile came from, where it flew on, but if you suggest that it ricochetted on the asphalt and that the damage can be seen on the house, then it would be logical that the incoming trajectory or the direction from which the projectile came is from the bottom of the photograph. If my colleagues wrote that, then this is what their writing says, but I cannot confirm any of that because I didn't go out to the site, nor can I deny it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see in this photograph that this hole was dug out because it has sharp edges? Would you agree that it was not caused by the impact of a shell but, rather, by digging?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me repeat once again. I wouldn't speculate or express any conjectures on the basis of this photograph because I'm not certain what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We have finished with this. Now we'll go back to something. Yesterday, I had to abandon a line of questioning because I had an inadequate map in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we now please see 1D722A. And just for your information, it was an incident in Dositejeva Street 224.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is not in e-court, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see 1D722 then? Maybe it's replaced. We had this map yesterday but it's too much enlarged, so obviously I'll have to return to that one again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll move on and go to incident in Mis Irbina 18. [Interpretation] For that we need something that you mentioned in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In B/C/S it's page 20, paragraph 66; and in English, it's page 11, paragraph 66.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say in your statement that in this incident, everything was caused by 120-millimetre shell, which was fired from the VRS position in Miljevici. You also told us that Mirza Jamakovic was killed in this incident. I apologise. Mirza Jamakovic's son was killed and his daughter, 14-year-old, was injured. This is mentioned in paragraph 67 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see 1D722 in e-court. In this case we will be able to work with this document. We just need to turn it around, this map, clockwise for 90 degrees, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark on this map -- I see here below Marsala Tita Street, Mis Irbina Street. Can you please mark the building number 18 Mis Irbina Street. There a letter P here; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second. [Marks]. It was around here, this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Would you now please mark the place where the security services centre is.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Across from there in Benovalencija. [Marks]. Somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you now please also draw a circle around the BiH Presidency, though we can see that it's written on the map.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where be the command of the 105th Motorised Brigade was located, in the Sipad building?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't know. All right. Do you know where the command of the 1st Corps of the BH Army was in Danijela Ozme?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went there. I know that it was located somewhere there in Danijela Ozme, but I wouldn't know in which specific building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we would need 1D721.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, yes, we have to have that admitted and it would be helpful if you invite the witness to put some letters next to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I told you I'm going to forget something.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Could you please write number 18 by the circle with which you marked Mis Irbina number 18?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And next to the circle with which you marked the Sarajevo CSB, just write CSB, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we have the last circle where we see the Presidency of BH. So there's no need to mark anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to tender the document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D722 as marked by the witness receives number D219, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I called up another document. The witness participated in its drafting. The document has not been translated. A translation is pending. We will use it only to establish that the witness did participate in the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 1 you see your name under number 6. Is that right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Judge Zdenko Eterovic heads the investigating team; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document we need page 13, which is a rough draft.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm just wondering which 65 ter number --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- English translation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or which one the -- it's not on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It should be 1D721.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, 1D721. It's not from the Prosecutor's list, it's our document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It was mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. It was mentioned, you said, "Now we could need 1D721" at page 53, line 12. It's clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please get a little context on the record in terms of what incident and what date this material relates to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, give me one second. It's paragraph 66 of witness's statement, and 67. It's Mis Irbina, 27th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the sketch is part of that report --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or is it separate?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is part of that report, page 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see that somebody used English to enter some data. I apologise. It is only in my version but not in the other. Please look at this schematic and mark -- and I repeat, this is a case that you participated in. Can you mark the bunker in front of the security services centre and subsequently we're also going to show a photo depicting that bunker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Lukic, could you first ask the witness to identify where the -- the building you are apparently referring to, where that is found on this sketch, if he knows. What is the sketch at all? I've got no idea yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one second. I'll try to find where the sketch --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see at least there seems to be some kind of a passage to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us see, maybe I rushed too much. Let's go back two pages. So go to page 11 first. I didn't want to bother Your Honours with the text since don't have the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Page 11 is a cover page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that this document depicts the place where the incident happened in Sarajevo in front of Mis Irbina Street number 15?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. Number 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that, that this schematic depicts shelling in Sarajevo in Mis Irbina Street in front of number 18?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I want to make things very clear for the Trial Chamber. This was not part of our report. It was part of the entire case. It was not us who drafted this drawing. It was the CSB who did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. Photos were taken on the 29th of June, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not participate in those activities, but if that is what it says, then I suppose that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the following page. Can we display it on the screen, please. Page 12. Zoom in on the lower part where it says "Description." "On 27 June 1995, at 1825 hundred hours, a mortar shell landed and exploded in the courtyard in front of the building at Mis Irbina Street number 18. The shell was fired from the aggressor's positions from the south-west direction. On that occasion Mirza Jamakovic was killed." Actually, I'm not sure about the first name. "Whereas Jasenkova -- Jasenka Jamakovic, Adi Habel, Milan Terzic, Davor Mitic, Vladimir Knezevic, and Alija Starogorac were seriously wounded."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you read "Vladimir Knezevic"? I see Davor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Davor. No, I said Davor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Davor Mitic. [In English] Then Knezevic Vladimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see, yes. I see Vladimir is without a W, yes, or a very small one, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you work on that incident?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the incident. I didn't draft the report. There is obviously a mistake here. It was not Mirza Jamakovic who was killed but Hariz, his son. And his daughter's name was Jesenka, not Jasenka as is stated in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, your mike is on. Do you want to ask something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I was just -- I was just wondering how we are going to proceed with all this. Is there any dispute as this is most likely is a report about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this appears to be a file with respect to this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution was -- suggests from proceeding and especially in terms of the questions that have been raised, that the parties discuss what parts of this file to tender, acquire translations for it, and then admit that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it is about a mortar, Mr. -- is that what you read, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I don't know what you want to do with it, but we are ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to go back to the drawing to ask the witness to mark some additional stuff on the drawing for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the drawing on page 13, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Coming after that page -- that, yeah, page number 12 with description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I've got no idea what it draws, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, in my previous question I did not -- or, rather, I was not very precise. The Judge insists on the location of the building at Mis Irbina 18. Can you mark that for us.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What are we looking at, streets or buildings or what are we looking at, Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This witness would say, "I didn't draw this," but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but I take it if you want to ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- those are buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to ask questions about it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I understand that those are ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see, for example, I see a shape, I don't know whether it's a building or not, which, forgive me, looks like a -- it looks like an ice cream on a -- what is that? It apparently hit something or not, or is that just a middle of the page --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I started with a building because you were interested in the building in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is then a building, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the building at Mis Irbina 18; right? Or 20, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but this is just one part of the building's wall. I encircled the entrance into the building from the side of the passage. To be more precise, this is the entrance into the building on the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the bigger circle with number 18.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you mark the smaller circle with the letter E standing for the English word "entrance," if you will.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now can you mark the building of the Sarajevo CSB, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether what we see here is the end of the CSB building or whether it is already the adjacent building. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you're not sure, don't mark anything.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't think that this is a part of the building. Currently there are some commercial premises on the right-hand side, and I believe that the adjacent building is the CSB building. I don't know whether they shared a wall or not. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the cone-shaped building or the ice cream-shaped building, would that represent a mortar shell? How do you understand this drawing?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know what the author of the drawing had in mind. Is there a description of -- anywhere? I don't know what is depicted in here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please put clear questions to the witness and -- because the witness apparently is a bit lost as well what it all presents. Either you introduce in such a way that it's clear to everyone or move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to the previous page, page 12. We will not keep this -- [In English] We'll have to come back anyways, first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But you will lose the markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will -- I will -- we'll make them again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're interested in the top part. We'll have to retain this in our memories, then I will jog your memory. Number 1 it the place where the shell landed, its crater; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Number 2 are traces of blood. Number 3, damage on the entrance door. There's no number 4. Number 5, again traces of blood. 6, traces of blood. Letter B, a sentry box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would suggest to put both on the screen, this list on the left side and the sketch on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That would be a good idea. Can we have it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, look at the drawing. Can you see number 1?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 is in a smudged area in the drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can you mark it? It's the place where the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you see number 3, damage on the entrance door?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see number 3, but I know what door you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Number 3 seems to be in a detail A, which is found to the -- at the right side of the sketch, and where it is a detail of is unclear to me yet, but if the witness could tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can't see number 3, but could you nevertheless mark the door. You've already done it before.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I will also include letter A. I'm sure that there must be a line leading from this letter A, but it's not visible in this copy of the drawing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a dotted line from that door going down to the right. It's a dotted very thin line, and it is then -- it seems that it -- where we have the cone, the top of the cone goes into the left then and further down. So I see a line, Mr. Lukic, but I have great difficulties yet in comparing the shape of the detail of A with what we find as number A on the sketch as a whole. It seems not to be much similarity. I don't know where the door is. I'm totally lost. And we are looking at this moment only at a part of the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the other part you just see that detail A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that's where we find the 2 and the 3, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if we are going through the legend, then we'd have to look at that as well. And then it says it's a detail of A. If we could move a little bit to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We cannot now move anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can not move at this moment because it's marked, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I will ask only one more question and then we'll go to that detail part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, look at the drawing and tell us whether you can mark the sentry box in the illustration key. It is under B.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see letter B, and I suppose that it refers to this part here. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Precisely so, and we will later see that in a photo which is also part of the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we tender this drawing with the witness's markings into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D721 as marked by the witness receives number D220, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted. Mr. Lukic, there seems to be also something under number 5 which is very difficult to read. 1, 2, 3, and 4 says "mjesta fotografisanja," and then there's a 5 which is not well legible. It looks like "pravac" or "pravas."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Incoming trajectory of the projectile." [In English] The direction of ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would rather have it translated by the booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see that. But is that a 5 or is that a -- or is that on a photograph number 5? I've got no idea. Could you please take care that we are assisted by the evidence and not confused by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the only version we found, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's about your organisation of the questions you put to the witness and the organisation by which you introduced this evidence to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask about this part at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are putting something to us where we have no idea what we are looking at, and if you want us to consider it in the interest of your client, then please present it in such a way --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying, Your Honour, but I'm working with the documents not composed by us. We are -- we have to use semi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it's a matter of being organised. That is it, nothing else, nothing more. Start with what we can understand. Put clear questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have 1D721, page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have just had 1D721. It's D220.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we had page 13. Now we have to have page 4, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 4. That's where the photographs are. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This bunker or guard post as it is referred to in the report is in the immediate vicinity of the explosion and marked accordingly in the sketch; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the guard post in front of the security services centre of the Ministry of the Interior in downtown Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the check-point where the policemen used to stand. I wouldn't call it a guard post, because all facilities secured by police have posts for a security person, and this one was secured against projectile impact with these sandbags.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to go back once again to the sketch now. So if we could please show page 13 of the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The children were in the entrance hall of the building which is marked here as detail A; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And if I may clarify a bit so as to make it clearer for the Trial Chamber. Numbers 5 and 6 are the markings for the places where traces of blood were found, and the following places are marked in such a way. [Marks]. 5 and 6 indicate those locations, but I do not see where the trajectory is drawn. Probably it cannot be seen on this copy. I can suppose where it had come from and where it is. We can discern something here, so that's probably the incoming trajectory of the projectile, but without the original drawing, it's difficult. And let me continue. Detail A indicates the entrance to the entry hallway where the children were injured and one of them killed, and that is here as we marked a while ago. [Marks]. That is the entrance. That was entry hall and the staircase inside the building. That was the entrance leading into the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, what you marked, and let's put an E to that for "Entrance." If you'd please be so kind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, apparently at the right lower part there is a detail sketch of what is A, and we find A where you earlier marked entrance. Now, I have difficulties in comparing the shape of what is found under detail A with what I see around where you marked it E for "Entrance." But perhaps first we should look at the text under the detail. Perhaps that may clarify something. Could we zoom in if its legible at all? No, we cannot zoom in. Mr. Lukic, it's just a matter of reading, and Mr. Weber has not objected yet. Can you tell us what approximately an arrow upwards and under that there is some text --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I cannot read this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You cannot read it. Then we will not know what it says. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before this is removed from the screen, can you please also draw a straight line from the place marked as the place of explosion in this drawing to the place where the entrance is and where the doors are through which one piece of shrapnel pierced according to the report?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Judge noticed this dotted line a while ago, and this is the line that indicates that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please just draw on top of it so that it's stronger and more visible, and please draw number 1 above the line. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The sketch of the site says the following: Someone read it and we can see here that the distance is 17.60 metres. Do you have any information about this? And your line, the line that you marked last, crossed the number now.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not doubt the measurements. It's around 15 metres from the place of the impact to the doors of the building. So that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, page of a report marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D221, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Could I ask the witness to look at it and perhaps have it enlarged slightly, the middle part. No, the middle part. That part, yes. Witness, do you see that apparently the dotted line does not only go downwards in -- to the right but then apparently at -- I don't know what it is, then goes back and is -- also there are two dotted lines, each of them apparently going to a place where traces of blood are found. Do you have any idea what -- is that also what you expect to be the trajectory of shrapnel after the explosion so that it would have caused the blood at 5 and the blood at 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The dotted lines show precisely the distance between the crater and the places where certain traces were found. 5 and 6 are traces of blood, and in the detail on the other side is the hole on the doors caused by the projectile which pierced through them. So the precise distances are marked here, and the shrapnel had the trajectory from the place of the impact to the door that was pierced by the shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means it follows the dotted line, unless it did not go in a straight line. Let's move on. I slowly start grabbing at least some of what it all presents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But could we also ask the witness, because that's still unclear, the -- the cone shape with the little Vs in the centre, what does that represent? You see it? It's a double line surrounded by an irregular shape and little Vs and at the top of it we find the impacts. Could you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I will try. I suppose, and we'll confirm that from the photographs if we have them, that it is a grass plot with no concrete, and I think that the little Vs stand for grass and that everything surrounding it is a concrete surface, but from this point in time I cannot really remember if this is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would everyone agree that it's quite common to use little Vs for grass? That is then one. And then I also see what looks as little -- possibly little cameras. Would that indicate how photographs were taken? I see two little structures, one facing, if I could say so, the door, the other one facing the grassy -- grassy patch. Would that be camera positions as far as you're aware of? And I see a few more on --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. We can find it on page -- which is prior to this page. On -- we have B, "strazarska kucica," [Interpretation] "guard post," [In English] and then we have and then I, II, III, IV, in Roman letters, places of taking pictures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that we -- in O, what seems -- looks like cameras. That we have numbers in it. I see a I, II, III, II and III close to each other, and most likely IV in the lower left part of the sketch. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But perhaps after the break, because it's time for a break. Mr. Lukic, if you would have carefully studied all the maps and the report, which I cannot study because it is not in a language I understand, all these matters like photographs, camera positions, grassy patch, et cetera, you could have introduced that in approximately five to seven minutes. We now spent approximately 45 minutes in total chaos, and we slowly now think that we understand some of it. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would just ask that 1D721, the entire file get marked for identification pending translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D721 receives OTP number or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we give it a Defence number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D222, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D222 is marked for identification. The witness may follow the usher. We'll take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you tell us how much time you think you would still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I will have to use all my time I asked, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but we'll consider -- we're also considering the way in which you used your time, and we'll also consider that all the time which is written down on our bill, to say so, that it's mainly to clarify what seems to be Defence evidence and just for the Chamber to make it digestible and, to that extent, assisting the Defence in presenting its evidence, and we'll consider that and I'll ask for a time report from Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to ask Your Honours that although this statement is pretty short, there are so many --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the only thing I'm talking about is the chaotic way in which you present all this at this moment. We take a break, and we resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, Mr. Lukic, could you explain in two or three lines what the purpose of your line of questioning at this moment is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We want to prove that a kid that died in this incident killed himself. Actually, he was playing with explosives given to him by his father, and it's obvious from the photographs there is only one fragment of the shell entered through that door allegedly killing him, destroying his face and wounding five other kids. According to us, it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's clear what you're heading for. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can take advantage of these free movements. Your Honour, the Prosecution is always looking for ways to reduce the size of its case and in discussing the matter of investigators from Sarajevo with members of the team, we've come to the conclusion that RM175, who is scheduled to testify at the end of next week is no longer necessary because many of the documents that we would have tendered through him have now been admitted in evidence. Your Honours, in an effort to ensure that next week is full, we will be endeavouring to advance RM013, who is scheduled the following week, that's week 24, into the end of next week. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll hear from the Defence whether there's any problem with this change in scheduling.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's hard for us to know at this moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll wait for you. You have an opportunity to think about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may now proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D721. We're interested in page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, what we can see here is a glass door; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it is a tin door.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. There's a number 3 here on page 12, and the key says that number 3 indicates the damage on the door, and we can see that there's one shrapnel trace on the door.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's just one shrapnel damage on the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that there's no damage on the wall, however?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right-hand side you can see some damage. This is a wall made of facade brick, so there is some damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark what you believe is damage on the wall.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will mark what I think is damage. [Marks]. And there are others somewhat smaller which I can't see, but I can't claim that there is no more damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up 1D724.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you asked about the one shrapnel damage on the door. I would like to be shown that. I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have marked one number we have on that door according to the official record made by CSB Sarajevo. They said one penetration. It's marked with one. If there was more, we would have more numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where is it on the door? I don't know. I can't read B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I trust them that there is one. I cannot even also see penetration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you were asking the witness if he could see the damage on the -- the one shrapnel damage on the door and he said yes. And I'm trying to find out which --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... it's above number 3 what I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, would it assist you, and we could not use this one, so let's have this one first out to look at page 7 of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But this should be tendered before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It should be tendered before. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before -- before it's tendered, maybe we can ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, can you mark the place where you see damage on the door?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We started saving already, so, Mr. Lukic, I suggest to you are -- it's gone. Yes. Witness, can you now mark where you see damage on the door, shrapnel damage, if you can see it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the quality of the photo is such that there -- that without the key under the photo and the number 3, I wouldn't be sure where damage is. However, under the photo it says that number 3 denotes damage on the entrance door probably caused by shrapnel. I can mark a little arrow above number 3 which probably points to the damage on the door. That's what I can mark. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think there's any need for having that marked. Well, you marked it already. Now you have a circle around the 3. Could you again make the marking you made earlier, that is the damage to the wall. Could you make that same marking again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The right marking is the damage on the wall, the marking on the 3 is the other one. Madam Registrar, this would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D223, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. Mr. Lukic, if it would assist you, you could consider 1D00721, page 7. But please proceed as you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I see nothing here. [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D724 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is the same door. The photo was taken in 2010, and it is the same wall. Do you agree with me that there's no visible damage in this photo?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. There is no noticeable damage, at least there's none in this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. My next question is this: Did you find any casualties, any victims when you got to the spot?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now we would like to see page 10 in 1D721.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we move, I would like to ask the witness in relation to this photograph on the screen, do you recognise that this is the same location as the door we have seen before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could assume that it's the same, but without the instructions, I can say that the door is different. The wall is the same. If we were to look at the photo independently, I could not confirm that it's the same place. I do not have any doubts that it is the same place, but the photo was taken much after the war. And it is true that this is the door to number 20 at the moment, as it is at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This door seems to be a door made of glass. The door you have seen earlier, you said it was made of tin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. During the war, there were very few glass surfaces which were intact. Most of those were damaged by war. I don't know what kind of door existed before the war. During the war the door was made of tin. It had a tin surface, not a glass surface.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And now I would like to call up page 10 in 1D721, but before that I would like to tender into evidence the document that we have just had on the screen, D1724.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D724 receives number D224, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D224 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Although the photos are black and white, and I know that it is not easy for you to be looking at the photos of your colleague's dead son, did you see Jamakovic at the time? Did you see what kind of injuries he had sustained?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see that in the black and white photos? I'm going to tell you that those injuries were caused by the explosion that happened in the vicinity of the child's face and not by shrapnel. Could you agree that that was the cause of his injuries and that five other children were injured by the shrapnel of a mortar shell which exploded 15 metres away?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that they were not hurt by one single shrapnel fragment. I don't know why you think that one single shrapnel fragment injured all of the children.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you. All of the children were indoors, behind the closed door, and it is stated that one shrapnel pierced the door. Do you think that more than one shrapnel pierced the door at the same time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that the door --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection to the form of the question. Counsel's essentially testifying and describing an event. If that is stated at a certain report or page, we just ask that the witness be allowed to see that before he comments on such a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before that, are these people lying on their side or are they standing? How are these photographs supposed to be? Are they okay like this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's a dead body. Dead body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, there are a lot of -- a lot of suggestions in your question. Could you explore with the witness to what extent he can verify the factual description you gave or put to him where it's found in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have just stated that you think that they could not have all been hurt by one piece of shrapnel. According to your information, were there more pieces of shrapnel that pierced the door? Is it not stated in the report?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any other information, but I don't know that the door was closed during the explosion. I never came by that information. I don't know whether the door was closed. It is possible that it was open, so there would be no shrapnel traces on the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can one expect that there would be no damage on the wall from a mortar shell that exploded 17 metres away, bar one that you noticed? Judging from your experience, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not establish the exact number of and extent of damage during the explosion. I would not go into speculation as to why we don't have sufficient information. Every projectile is tested during the manufacture process for the number of pieces of shrapnel that will be caused by its explosion. I don't know -- I'm not sure that any analysis based on the information that we have at our disposal would yield the correct result. What we saw in that photo is a door and a very narrow strip of wall around the door. What went on around the area, behind the door, we can't see and there is no way for us to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please look at the screen in front of you. The photos are black and white. If we're talking about a mortar shell shrapnel, can it cause this type of injury which Jamakovic sustained and which caused his death, or would it be more consistent with an explosion of an explosive device which was in his hands, perhaps, or in his very close vicinity?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information available to me, the boy died of shrapnel wounds. I can't conclude that based on these photos. The photos are blurred, and I don't want to go into analysing something that I can hardly see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we're talking about mortar shells, an 82 mortar shell, how many pieces of shrapnel is it fragmented into?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't even give you an approximate number. I don't want to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now just bear with me for a moment, please. Let's go to the flea market in Bascarsija. You've already testified about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need P12822 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think instead of P it should be a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is 65 ter, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You drive us to P numbers well over 10000, which scares us a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 12822. That's what we have on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English we need page 1, and in the B/C/S version we need page 5, bullet point 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is to demonstrate that you were indeed a member of the team. It is stated here following the information: An on-site commission was formed, and under number 4 we see your name; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Allow me to retract a little and go back to the questions relative to the late Jamakovic. If you found any shrapnel that injured the children and killed Jamakovic, was that documented in any way?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received shrapnel for analysis, and that was described in our analysis. I don't know if any shrapnel was extracted from the dead boy's body.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This was just a little digression. I'm going back to the flea market from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need the same document, page 9 in B/C/S, the penultimate and final paragraphs, and in English page 4, two paragraphs from the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You signed this report on the expert analysis?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with my initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To say for the record it happens in Telali Street, which was formerly called Petra Kocica; correct? You can see it here.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the report mentions the name of the street at the relevant time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We now need to see the sketch which does not exist in the English version, so we do not need any page from that version. We need the sketch on page 17 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As these were two shells, could you please mark for us in this sketch the places where the shells fell. We can see one down here.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One explosion, but there is no key.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. First we should show the key. It is my mistake and thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The key can be found on page 16 of the B/C/S version and at page 7 of the English version. We can see what the key says. I will read it now. Number 1, location of explosion of one of the projectiles in front of a shop. Under number 2, location where the other projectile was activated at the curb of Oprkanj Street. Number 9, fragment of a projectile fuse; 06 and 30 [as interpreted], projectile fragments, and then under 10 and 11, projectile fragments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, looking at the English version and the original version, there seems to be quite a difference. Unless it is not the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is the same page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, for example, in the English, 12 is missing where it clearly appears in the original. 06 and 30 appear after 9, before 10. It doesn't appear in English. Therefore, I think if this is a Prosecution uploaded document, we should have the translation be verified. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we now please move on to the sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the meantime, we should make a correction of the transcript. Page 79, line 14, I think it was one of the interpreters misspoke. You are dealing with number 1 fragment of a projectile fuse, number 6 and 13 but it's written "30," which is obviously a mistake. It should read "13."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. [Interpretation] Can we now move it a little bit just -- or we can see everything in the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see numbers 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These are -- let us focus on number 1. If you can mark it and explain what sort of an explosion that was.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is number 1. This is the explosion right next to the wall of a building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And number 2 as well, please. Just mark it so that it will be easier for you to follow.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is the place where the projectile impacted against the curb.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under number 9, it's said that this was the fuse.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the body of the fuse. That is the place where the body of the fuse was located. It was found at this spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Next to number 1 at the top of the sketch there is no crater. No crater is documented. And the fuse, can you determine first of all what was the direction from which those shells came?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I can confirm that there were craters in both locations. Now, whether this is documented or not ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where did these shells come from?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately from this direction. [Marks]. Whether it was perhaps a little bit to the left or to the right, that's a different thing, but the angle is precisely determined in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The fuse marked with number 9 is oriented in the opposite direction from the direction that the shell came from. Isn't that what's documented here?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is located next to number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would suggest to you that this is impossible. Would you agree with me that it is impossible for a fuse to be found in the place showing the direction from which the shell flew?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the projectile which is marked by number 1 -- or, rather, the place of its impact, it impacted in the place at the bottom of the wall of this building, just next to the ground. So it's not impossible that many pieces of shrapnel bounced off the wall and flew back, and the same goes for the fuse. So this is how the fuse came to be in the location where it was found.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. It is the end of our time for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask one additional question in relation to this. There is an arrow with an N on the top of the building. Does that mean that the top of the building is north, the top of the sketch is north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore the shells came from approximately the southerly direction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps south-eastern direction, but the angle is included in the report. As far as I remember, it was south-east but it's specified in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before we break, I would just ask to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, sketch marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sketch marked by the witness receives number D225, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D225 is admitted into evidence. We adjourn for the day. I'd like to instruct you, Witness, that you should not speak or communicate in any other way with whomever about your testimony, whether already given yesterday and today or still to be given tomorrow, because we're quite confident that we'll conclude your testimony tomorrow. You may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and we resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 13th of February, in -- at 9.30 in the morning in this same Courtroom I.
